title: QUIC RFC 9000 Server Refusal And 0-RTT Pre-Initial Buffering Work Item
summary: Close the remaining RFC 9000 Section 5.2.2 server pre-acceptance tail for deliberate connection refusal and limited 0-RTT buffering before a matching Initial arrives.
planned_changes:
- Emit a protected Initial CONNECTION_CLOSE with CONNECTION_REFUSED when the listener application deliberately refuses an otherwise valid new connection.
- Unregister provisional endpoint routes when admission fails before the connection is accepted.
- Add a bounded listener-local 0-RTT pre-Initial buffer keyed by Initial Destination Connection ID.
- Drain buffered 0-RTT datagrams into endpoint routing after the matching Initial is admitted.
- Add focused requirement-home tests and canonical trace links for S5P2P2 0007 and 0008.
verification_plan: Run a Release build, run the focused S5P2P2 0007/0008 requirement-home filter, run the full S5P2P2 requirement-home filter, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and check the diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: 0-RTT decryption, early-data acceptance, anti-replay policy, or application delivery.
Client-side Version Negotiation handling or Initial/Retry connection-ID continuity.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused listener pre-acceptance tail over QuicListenerHost, QuicListenerPreAcceptanceIngressPolicy, QuicListenerZeroRttPreInitialBuffer, and S5P2P2 requirement-home tests.
